reader.requirement: At --std 85 CHAR's argument-1 must be an integer argument (§1989:A.2.2 AR4) and every non-integer form is refused; an integer argument yields the character at that ordinal position of the program collating sequence.

reader.edition-search: Read Violation, IntegerViolation, NonIntegralItemReason and the NotAlwaysIntegral walk, CheckArgumentClasses and BindFunctionResult; grepped IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs and IntrinsicBinder.cs for Edition/DialectLevel/CobolVersion/AppliesAt/IntroducedIn. reader.notes: CHAR's argument-1 goes through the same integer screen at --std 85 as at 2023: scaled items, non-integral literals, numeric functions, quotients not provably integral, alphanumeric items, groups and ALL literals are refused, and integer items, expressions and integer functions are admitted with correct results. Diagnostics at --std 85 cite §2023:15.15.3 r1.

refuter.evidence: fn_edge.cob at --std 85: MOVE FUNCTION CHAR(N * (N - 1) / 2 + 65) TO C refused, 'error COBOL1627: FUNCTION CHAR argument-1 is an arithmetic expression whose term (N * (N - 1)) is an integer under the net factor 0.5 ...'; N * (N - 1) is always even, so the argument always results in an integer value and §1989:A.2.9.3 AR1 with §1989:A.2.2 AR4 makes it legal. Same at --std 2023. Admitted and correct: CHAR(ORD-MAX(1 2) + 64) = A and CHAR(PP * 6 + 6) over PIC 9P = A (fn_legal2.cob). Refused correctly: CHAR(MIDRANGE(64 66)), CHAR(MEDIAN(64 66)). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.9.3 AR1 'Argument-1 must be an integer'; OK §1989:A.2.2 AR4.
